corpusSummary: Across 40+ records, the corpus reveals a landscape where Large Language Models intersect with human decision-making, health, education, policy, and culture. Recurring themes include evaluating real-world AI use, social trust and embodiment, LLMs as research tools requiring validation, and persistent concerns about bias, ethics, and sustainability. Findings depict varied adoption, context-dependent trust, and a strong call for governance and human oversight.

themes.name: Human–AI interaction, trust, and embodiment
themes.description: Explores how users perceive, trust, and interact with AI agents, including embodiment, empathy, privacy, and social influence, across consumer, educational, and health contexts.

themes.name: LLMs as research tools and governance
themes.description: Examines methodological opportunities, validation challenges, multi-agent simulations, and governance frameworks for responsible use of LLMs in social science research.

themes.name: AI in health, wellbeing, and education
themes.description: Investigates AI-driven health information, patient education, counseling, and AI-enhanced learning and literacy, highlighting safety, accuracy, engagement, and equity considerations.

themes.name: AI in policy, culture, heritage, and inequality
themes.description: Covers AI-enabled public participation, policy analysis, climate and ESG implications, heritage preservation, digital humanities, and the digital divide shaping adoption and outcomes.
